description: Bandpassed noise gated by four staggered envelopes, so one hit sounds like several hands, in the manner of the 808 clap

params.text: Sets the decay of the first three envelopes together, 10ms fully anticlockwise to 20ms fully clockwise; the manual says 5ms to 15ms
Sets when the second, third and fourth envelopes fire after the trigger: the second from 20ms to 40ms, the third from 35ms to 50ms and the fourth from 45ms to 60ms
Sets the centre of the bandpass filter on the noise, 800Hz to 1600Hz; the tooltip and the manual say the top is 16000Hz
Sets the decay of the fourth envelope, 20ms to 100ms, which is the tail heard as a room
Sets how much of the fourth envelope's noise reaches the mix; fully anticlockwise removes the tail
Multiplies the mix by 1 up to 10 before the output clips at 5V, so turning it up squares the noise off
Fires the clap; a rising edge at the trigger jack does it too

inputs.text: A rising edge above 0.5V fires the sound; the length of the gate makes no difference
Adds to the VERB DECAY knob
Adds to the VERB VOLUME knob

notes: a CV input is bipolar and is added to its knob: 10V there is worth the knob's whole travel, -10V cancels a knob that is fully up, and the total is clamped to the knob's own range
only the first envelope fires with the trigger; the other three are started by a sample count, so a second trigger before the spread has run cancels whichever have not fired yet
all four envelopes gate the same piece of filtered noise, so the four hands are the same hand at four moments
